findings.title: Upsampling eligibility check uses wrong dataset variable
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, the eligibility check `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` is called with the outer closure variable `dataset` instead of the function's own `scoped_dataset` parameter, which is the dataset actually used to execute the query (`scoped_dataset.timeseries_query(...)`, `scoped_dataset.top_events_timeseries(...)`, etc.). In the dashboard-widget discover-split code path (`get_event_stats_factory`), `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `scoped_dataset` values such as `discover` for error-only/transaction-only sub-queries while the outer `dataset` variable remains something else (e.g. `metrics_performance`/`metrics_enhanced_performance`). Because `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` branches on the dataset argument passed in, this mismatch causes upsampling to be incorrectly enabled/disabled for these split sub-queries, producing wrong (un-upsampled or incorrectly-upsampled) counts for dashboard widgets.

findings.title: upsampled_count() changes result meta type for the same field name
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQL function is aliased as `count` by `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` ("upsampled_count() as count") but declares `default_result_type="number"`, whereas the standard `count()` function used elsewhere returns `default_result_type="integer"`. Since the field name exposed to API consumers is identical (`count`), clients that rely on a stable meta type for this field will now see different types depending on whether the querying org/projects happen to be on the error-upsampling allowlist, which is a silent, data-dependent API contract change that can break strict type-based response parsing.

findings.title: Option key used but registration not shown in this PR
findings.body: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` calls `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])`. Nowhere in this PR's changed files is this option registered (e.g. via `options.register(...)` in options defaults). If this option is not already registered elsewhere in the codebase, calling `options.get()` on an unregistered key will raise at runtime and break every call to `get_event_stats` (since this check now runs unconditionally for every event-stats request). This should be verified/confirmed before merge.

findings.title: Cache key built from Python's built-in hash() of project id tuple
findings.body: The cache key `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"` relies on the built-in `hash()` of a tuple to disambiguate different project-id sets. This is fragile: hash collisions between different project-id tuples (however unlikely) would cause one project set's eligibility result to be served for a different project set under the same organization, silently enabling/disabling upsampling incorrectly. A deterministic, collision-free key (e.g. a stable string built directly from the sorted ids) would be safer than relying on `hash()`.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called anywhere
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined to keep the 60-second eligibility cache consistent with allowlist option changes, but nothing in this PR (or apparently the rest of the codebase, based on the changed files) calls it when the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option is updated. As written, the cache will always rely purely on the 60-second TTL for consistency, making this function dead code that implies a staleness-mitigation mechanism that doesn't actually exist yet.

findings.title: Docstring contradicts the caching behavior added in the same PR
findings.body: The docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` states "This function reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time, which means it can return different results between calls if the configuration changes during request processing." This is misleading: the caller (`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`) wraps this function behind a 60-second cache specifically to avoid calling it on every request, so the claim of per-call freshness no longer holds once cached.

findings.title: Transform only matches exact 'count()' string, silently skips other forms
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only transforms a column when `column.lower().strip() == "count()"`. Any aliased form (e.g. `count() as total`) or equation referencing count is left untouched with no warning or logging, so users querying with a slightly different but semantically equivalent column string will silently get un-upsampled results while believing upsampling is enabled for their allowlisted project, with no indication of the mismatch.

findings.title: Shared store_event() test factory now silently mutates sample_rate for all callers
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` is unconditionally invoked on every call to `Factories.store_event`, and if `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` is present in the event payload for any reason, it overwrites `normalized_data["sample_rate"]`. This is a broad, implicit behavior change to a widely-used test helper; any existing or future test that sets this context field for unrelated purposes will now have its `sample_rate` silently altered. Errors during lookup/conversion are caught with a bare `except Exception: pass`, which will mask bugs (e.g. malformed contexts) rather than surfacing them in tests.

findings.title: Stray git submodule reference committed
findings.body: A new file `sentry-repo` was added containing only a subproject commit reference (`Subproject commit a5d290951def84...`), which looks like an accidental git submodule addition rather than an intentional change. This is unrelated to the feature being implemented and could break checkouts/CI for other contributors or indicate a broken local repository state that should not be merged.

findings.title: No tests for the caching entry point or cache invalidation
findings.body: The tests cover the private helper functions (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`) but never test the main public entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, which contains the new caching logic (cache hit/miss, TTL behavior) that this PR's description specifically calls out as a 'performance optimization.' There is also no test for `invalidate_upsampling_cache`. Given the caching logic is the novel/riskiest part of this change, its absence from the test suite is a significant gap.
